instruction.text: A local theme park wants to track how long it takes one of their rollercoasters to travel 1,000 metres. This distance-time graph is supposed to show the time taken by a rollercoaster over its 1,000-metre track, but there are two issues with the graph. Select the two problems with the distance-time graph.

b: The graph has the same metre value twice at different times.
++The time and distance are on the wrong axes.
++There is a line missing between 15 and 20 seconds.

instruction.text: A local theme park wants to track how long it takes one of their rollercoasters to travel 1,000 metres. This time graph shows the time taken by a rollercoaster over its 1,000-metre track. Answer the questions using the distance-time graph.

atoms.a: How many metres long is the rollercoaster ride?
How far did the rollercoaster travel between 30 and 45 seconds?
How long did it take for the rollercoaster to travel 800 metres?
How far did the rollercoaster travel between 5 and 30 seconds?

instruction.text: Decide if a distance-time graph would be useful in these scenarios.

atoms.a: Mandy wants to track how many eggs she cooks each day.
Amy wants to see how fast she can run 1,000 metres.
Dave wants to know everybody’s favourite breakfast cereal.
Pete wants to see how fast he can throw a ball.
